design_contract.concurrency_protocol: snapshot observes a stable store image without adding allocations or synchronization to the publish hot path; restore builds validated replacement state off to the side, rejects concurrent mutation according to existing store lifecycle rules, and publishes the replacement atomically after full validation and cursor reconciliation.
forbidden_alternatives: Do not replay the entire journal as the primary cold-start restore path when a valid snapshot exists.
Do not mutate live store state before full snapshot validation completes.
Do not trust snapshot headers without magic, version, store metadata, and completeness validation.
Do not ignore per-page CRC mismatches or downgrade them to partial restores.
Do not allocate on the publish hot path to support snapshot metadata.
Do not expose staged-but-unjournaled writes after restore.
hard_constraints: Zero allocation on the publish hot path remains invariant.
qa/smoke.sh must pass the allocation gate.
Restore latency must be below 10ms p99 for a 1M-key snapshot.
SINGLE and DOUBLE direct stores must support snapshot and restore.
SINGLE and DOUBLE mmap stores must support snapshot and restore.
Restore must not surface staged-but-unjournaled writes until the guaranteed journal cursor is reconciled.
All invalid snapshot restore attempts must leave live state unchanged.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: store/ owns snapshot file format, CRC validation, direct/mmap state capture, atomic swap, and structured invariant failures; guaranteed-* owns journal cursor reconciliation contracts only where existing integration requires it; benchmarks/ owns restore latency measurement; QA/test roots own acceptance fixtures and regression coverage.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: snapshot writes to a temporary file, fsyncs data and parent directory where supported, then atomically moves into place; restore reads and validates magic, version, store kind, dimensions, page CRCs, completeness, and journal cursor before mutating live state; any stale, invalid, CRC-failed, or partial input returns a structured invariant failure with no live state mutation.
